one_line: Collaborative travel planner coordinating lodging, transport, attractions, and human-approved bookings through WebMCP.
what_it_does: Maintains shared trip context and orchestrates travel research and booking decisions across specialized panels.
leverage_rationale: Structured shared state and orchestration are useful, but the packet does not show why a general agent driving a travel UI could not achieve much of the same result.
leverage_evidence: Devpost preview visibly labels a WebMCP orchestrator and real-time sync.
UI shows shared destination, dates, budget, panels, and human-in-the-loop booking state.
execution_rationale: The polished embedded UI suggests a plausible product, but there is no submitted frame sheet or video transcript and the screenshot is packaging with a paused preview.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot shows populated travel panels, chat input, booking/status cards, and telemetry label.
No direct completed interaction or live tool result is visible.
impact_rationale: Travelers and families have a clear coordination problem, and the product addresses research, logistics, and safety in one shared workflow.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets accommodations, multimodal transport, local attractions, and culinary planning.
Human approval is explicitly retained for bookings.
creativity_rationale: A thoughtful synthesis of collaborative travel planning, bilingual context, and agent orchestration, though the category and interaction model are familiar.
creativity_evidence: Bilingual toggle, live collaboration, and human-in-the-loop booking are visible in the preview.
usability_note: The preview presents clear categories and a chat entry point, but live usability is not demonstrated.
red_flags: No submitted video frame sheets or transcript.
Devpost screenshot is packaging evidence, not runtime proof.
standouts: Shared travel context across multiple planning domains.
Human approval is integrated into the booking concept.
advance_reason: Promising concept and credible UI, but evidence is too thin for the next stage.

one_line: Solar sizing simulator where an agent searches thousands of panel, battery, and inverter configurations against constraints.
what_it_does: Lets humans tune solar assumptions while a structured agent search returns and visualizes optimized system tradeoffs.
leverage_rationale: The core value is an agent capability the UI cannot practically provide: exhaustive constrained search over a multi-dimensional design space rather than one-slider-at-a-time exploration.
leverage_evidence: Pitch states one WebMCP call evaluates roughly 2,000 configurations in-browser.
Preview visibly shows an agent sweep, configuration controls, tradeoff charts, and telemetry.
execution_rationale: The populated simulator, charts, metrics, and sweep visualization make the central workflow coherent and substantially evidenced, though the paused packaging view cannot independently verify the runtime claim.
execution_evidence: Preview shows 6x480 W panels, 3 kWh battery, inverter/load inputs, generation-versus-load chart, KPI cards, and a 10,372-configuration sweep.
One gallery image and three frame sheets show the product/dashboard states.
impact_rationale: Homeowners and solar designers have a concrete, consequential optimization problem, and the tool directly exposes cost, payback, self-sufficiency, and grid dependence tradeoffs.
impact_evidence: Product supports realistic daily load and load-shape assumptions.
Output metrics visibly include annual cost, self-sufficiency, payback, and cost per kWh.
creativity_rationale: It applies WebMCP to computational design-space exploration rather than form filling, with a memorable and well-matched interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Project explicitly contrasts agent search with human slider exploration.
Agent sweep visualization makes the new capability legible.
usability_note: Human sliders and charts provide an understandable fallback while the agent handles optimization.
red_flags: Exact 40 ms and 2,000-configuration claims are not independently verifiable from stills.
standouts: WebMCP changes the feasible problem, not merely the speed of UI interaction.
Strong visual alignment between inputs, agent sweep, and decision metrics.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage with strong visible execution and a concrete high-value use case.

one_line: Live marketplace that dynamically turns settled paid APIs into callable WebMCP tools.
what_it_does: Queries a trust-ranked Bazaar and registers tools for APIs with real x402/USDC settlement history, enabling agent payments.
leverage_rationale: The marketplace-to-tool pipeline and payment enforcement could make capabilities discoverable and callable without bespoke registration, beyond ordinary UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Pitch says every paid API becomes a callable WebMCP tool automatically.
Description claims tools are generated from live settlement and trust data rather than a frozen specification.
execution_rationale: The frame sheets show a marketplace, live runner, developer console, and tool invocation interface, but text and exact returned payloads are difficult to verify.
execution_evidence: Frames show Live API marketplace/Live Runner tools, tool cards, code/console panels, and invocation controls.
Devpost screenshot shows a titled WebMCP demo but paused media.
impact_rationale: Agent payments and automated access to paid APIs address a real infrastructure gap for API sellers and agent builders.
impact_evidence: Project describes live endpoints, on-chain USDC settlement, trust ranking, and seller/developer workflows.
Visible demo branding identifies x402, Bazaar, and on-chain enforcement.
creativity_rationale: Dynamic tool creation from real economic settlement is an unusually ambitious and memorable agent-infrastructure concept.
creativity_evidence: Marketplace itself writes the tool surface.
Combines payments, trust, settlement history, and WebMCP discovery.
usability_note: The developer-facing runner is visible, but the low-resolution frames do not establish how easy seller or agent use is.
red_flags: About text describes a broader stack built for months, suggesting the WebMCP entry may be an extension of pre-existing infrastructure.
Exact tool results are not legible.
standouts: Strongest conceptual bridge between real payments and dynamic agent capability discovery.
advance_reason: Highly original, high-leverage infrastructure with credible but not fully legible execution evidence.

one_line: Contractor field-proof workspace that checks job photos and records before preparing a handoff packet.
what_it_does: Combines workday records, dated photos, notes, and agent-assisted checks while leaving updates for contractor review.
leverage_rationale: An agent can inspect structured job records and prepare a coherent handoff more reliably than manual browsing, but the delta over ordinary browser operation is not fully shown.
leverage_evidence: Description says the agent checks records, finds missing information, and prepares updates.
Preview shows photo proof, timestamp, photo ID, and a human confirmation warning.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent contractor workflow and three frame sheets with a populated project record, but no clearly visible final handoff completion.
execution_evidence: Frames show Maple Street Kitchen Demo with dated entries, photos, and detail panels.
Devpost preview shows photo-check-passed state and approval controls.
impact_rationale: Small contractors have a concrete documentation and handoff burden; consolidating photo proof and daily records can deliver direct operational value.
impact_evidence: Product targets work photos, completed work, daily notes, corrections, approvals, and printable handoff packets.
Visible construction project records and photo evidence.
creativity_rationale: Useful and practical, but largely a conventional field-service/project documentation workflow with agent assistance.
creativity_evidence: Human review gate and photo-proof checks add a meaningful angle, but the concept remains familiar.
usability_note: The project record and proof-oriented layout are understandable, though the full handoff flow is not shown.
red_flags: Frame sheets mainly show inspection and scrolling, not a completed saved handoff.
Exact tool calls are not visible.
standouts: Clear target audience and practical workflow.
Human confirmation of photo evidence avoids unsafe automatic approval.
advance_reason: Credible practical product, but leverage and end-to-end evidence are moderate.

one_line: Transfers a human-demonstrated workflow between structurally different WebMCP sites using provenance-backed intent contracts.
what_it_does: Extracts intent from a source demonstration, maps it to a destination’s capabilities, adapts or queues ambiguous rules, and prepares a human-reviewed draft.
leverage_rationale: It replaces brittle click replay with semantic translation across sites, preserving, adapting, rejecting, and escalating intent based on destination capabilities.
leverage_evidence: Transcript reports 5 preserved, 2 adapted, 1 excluded, and 1 ambiguous rule.
Frames visibly show WebMCP tools discovered: inspect source, inspect compatibility, prepare draft, save contract.
execution_rationale: The video transcript provides an unusually specific end-to-end narrative and frame sheets show the workbench, event stream, DevTools discovery, and compatibility state; final save is less clearly evidenced.
execution_evidence: 91-second video transcript describes source demonstration, provenance review, destination mapping, human queue, and prepared draft.
Frames show Intent Relay Workbench, Orbit Events, console tool discovery, and capability map/Human Queue UI.
impact_rationale: People and organizations repeating workflows across web tools have a real portability problem; explicit ambiguity handling and human review make the proposed solution credible.
impact_evidence: Product transfers approved intent across Gather and Orbit with visibly different capabilities.
Publishing remains human-only and ambiguous mappings stop for a decision.
creativity_rationale: The concept and interaction model are genuinely novel: provenance-backed intent translation rather than automation replay.
creativity_evidence: Semantic rules cite the demonstration actions that justify them.
Visible preserved/adapted/non-transferable/human-queue distinctions are memorable and coherent.
usability_note: Rule-by-rule review and explicit human queue support safe use, though cross-site setup may be complex.
red_flags: Still frames do not prove the final contract save, though the transcript describes the draft endpoint.
standouts: Best evidence-backed semantic transfer model in the packet.
Strong safety behavior: no silent invention when a capability is missing or ambiguous.
advance_reason: Top-tier leverage and creativity with unusually strong, specific end-to-end evidence.

one_line: Human-approved spatial-repair rehearsal for temporary layouts with deterministic checks, stale-patch rejection, and verification receipts.
what_it_does: Lets an agent inspect a layout, run route/accessibility checks, stage ghost geometry, and propose an exact revision that only a person can approve.
leverage_rationale: Typed tools, shared revision state, deterministic checks, proposal hashes, and stale-patch rejection make agent collaboration materially safer and more reliable than DOM automation.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies five typed tools, shared command layer, revision-bound proposals, and SHA-256 receipts.
Human approval is UI-only; agents cannot approve their own patches.
execution_rationale: The design is technically coherent and detailed, but the packet has no video frames and the only image is a Devpost page whose embedded media is blocked.
execution_evidence: About text describes deterministic A* checks, atomic apply, rerun verification, and no-server deployment.
Devpost screenshot explicitly shows embedded-content security restriction, so runtime is not visible.
impact_rationale: Temporary clinics and similar spaces face real route and accessibility risks under time pressure; a controlled rehearsal and verification loop can prevent costly layout errors.
impact_evidence: Project targets blocked routes, pinch points, inaccessible destinations, and obstructions.
Failure-and-recovery scenario includes a stale proposal after a human lock change.
creativity_rationale: The stale-patch, hash-bound, human-approved spatial repair model is a fresh and ambitious application of WebMCP safety semantics.
creativity_evidence: Ghost geometry, revision/hash binding, and post-apply verification receipt form a distinctive interaction model.
usability_note: The approval and rehearsal framing is clear, but no runtime screens are available to judge operational ergonomics.
red_flags: No frame sheets or transcript; embedded demo blocked by connection-security restriction.
Claims are largely narrative rather than observed.
standouts: Excellent safety and concurrency model for agent-proposed spatial changes.
Clear separation between proposing and approving.
advance_reason: Exceptional concept, but execution evidence is too thin and the embedded demo is inaccessible.

one_line: Visual sign-to-place grounding that turns a storefront photo and location hint into OCR and ranked business candidates.
what_it_does: Analyzes uploaded signs, extracts text, searches place candidates, and returns grounded businesses with maps, images, addresses, and categories.
leverage_rationale: Agents receive structured visual/OCR/place-grounding operations that are difficult to reproduce reliably through generic UI driving, especially with multimodal evidence and ranked candidates.
leverage_evidence: Three named WebMCP tools are specified: get sign context, analyze sign, and get place candidates.
Frames show WebMCP Inspector execution with structured JSON-like output on a live business page.
execution_rationale: The frame sheets visibly show upload, location hint, OCR, candidate cards, and a WebMCP inspector execution flow, although exact payloads are not legible.
execution_evidence: Frames show Chicken Plus sign, Nha Trang hint, Analyze with GoPic, detected text, and candidate places.
Inspector frames show a named tool, Execute Tool control, parameters, and structured output.
impact_rationale: Travelers and field researchers often encounter businesses from imperfect signage; grounding OCR to place candidates addresses a real ambiguity problem.
impact_evidence: Candidate results combine OCR, geographic hint, maps, venue photos, addresses, and categories.
The visible Chicken Plus 0515 result demonstrates a concrete use case.
creativity_rationale: The sign-to-place workflow is a fresh synthesis of visual evidence, location context, and agent-callable grounding, though visual search itself is established.
creativity_evidence: Explicit separation of OCR from place grounding and candidate ranking.
WebMCP exposure makes the visual workflow directly agent-usable.
usability_note: The upload, hint, analyze, and candidate-card flow is legible and actionable.
red_flags: About text says GoPic already existed as a mobile visual-search product, so the WebMCP work is an extension.
standouts: Strong multimodal evidence chain from sign to grounded place.
Inspector frames visibly demonstrate real tool execution and structured results.
advance_reason: Strong evidence and a meaningful agent-specific multimodal workflow.

one_line: In-browser agent video editor that trims dead air, searches narration, places footage, and meets a runtime target without uploads.
what_it_does: Shares a timeline and activity history between human edits and agent operations, using transcript-aware placement and duration optimization.
leverage_rationale: Structured timeline, transcript, and media state let the agent perform constraint-satisfying edits precisely; generic UI driving would be substantially more brittle for this workflow.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies inspect timeline, detect dead air, search transcript, place footage, trim clips, add zooms, and optimize duration tools.
Frames show checked Agent Activity entries for phrase search at 17.4s, clip placement, trimming, and preview.
execution_rationale: Three frame sheets show a coherent editor and auditable activity log with concrete edits and preview state; the final export is not shown.
execution_evidence: Activity log visibly records media processing, word cuts, timeline dragging, target duration, phrase search, and terminal placement.
Devpost preview shows timeline/editor UI and the project claims a 108.7-to-60-second optimization.
impact_rationale: Content creators and product teams have a real tedious editing problem, especially when footage is sensitive and should stay local.
impact_evidence: Product targets dead-air trimming and transcript-to-footage synchronization.
No-upload/local-browser privacy claim directly addresses unreleased screen recordings.
creativity_rationale: The combination of local browser editing, narration-aware placement, shared human/agent history, and explicit duration optimization is ambitious and distinctive.
creativity_evidence: Agent Activity makes edits auditable in plain language while preserving human timeline edits.
Phrase-to-footage synchronization is a memorable workflow.
usability_note: A familiar timeline plus plain-English activity feed makes agent edits reviewable.
red_flags: Frame sheets show preview/activity but not a final exported file or independently verified no-upload behavior.
standouts: Strong product-specific use of structured timeline state.
Auditable shared activity history bridges human and agent editing.
advance_reason: High practical value, strong visible execution, and meaningful WebMCP leverage.

one_line: Persistent decision spaces where humans and agents collaborate on evidence, graphs, runs, and approval-gated organizational work.
what_it_does: Exposes shared Spaces, artifacts, participants, decision graphs, agent runs, messages, and human approval policies to an external agent through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP provides a bounded, typed bridge from an agent conversation into persistent shared work and approval state, beyond scraping a dashboard.
leverage_evidence: Pitch describes 54 WebMCP tools and a human approval requirement before execution.
Preview shows Supplier Launch Decision, Spaces, Runs, artifacts, and Approve/Deny controls.
execution_rationale: Frame sheets show an agent interacting with a Sentry-like shared workspace and producing a structured research/result flow, but exact Swarm tool calls and final artifact details are not legible.
execution_evidence: Frames show dark agent panel, Swarm/Sentry-like workspace, navigation, issue/detail inspection, and final green completion-style state.
Devpost screenshot shows an approval-gated Supplier Launch Decision demo preview.
impact_rationale: Persistent evidence, specialist agents, asynchronous runs, and accountable human decisions address consequential team and operations workflows.
impact_evidence: Description names supplier evidence artifacts, unresolved compliance claim, verification run, durable status message, and approval policy.
Product explicitly targets organizational work rather than a one-off chatbot response.
creativity_rationale: The Space and Decision Graph model is an ambitious interaction pattern for model-agnostic human-agent collaboration, though adjacent orchestration systems exist.
creativity_evidence: Persistent spaces combine evidence, graphs, participants, runs, and policy.
External ChatGPT conversation can continue work inside a durable artifact space.
usability_note: Spaces and approval controls provide a clear collaboration frame, but the breadth of the system may increase complexity.
red_flags: Frame content is low-resolution and partially resembles adjacent Sentry/research interfaces, limiting exact attribution.
About text presents a broad pre-existing platform with a challenge-specific WebMCP layer.
standouts: Human approval is central rather than ornamental.
advance_reason: High impact and strong agent-infrastructure concept with moderate visual execution evidence.

one_line: Agent-mediated resale negotiation where buyer and seller agents bargain and humans approve the final deal.
what_it_does: Provides product and offer information to agents, supports negotiation on both sides, and gates completion on human approval or configured auto-approval.
leverage_rationale: Structured offers and a human approval gate can make negotiation repeatable, but the packet does not establish a major advantage over a general agent using a marketplace UI.
leverage_evidence: Description says WebMCP tools provide all information to buyer and seller agents.
Devpost preview visibly shows agent activity, offers, market information, and approval controls.
execution_rationale: The dashboard preview indicates a plausible negotiation product, but there are no frame sheets, transcript, or visible completed deal result.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot shows a titled WebMCP resale-platform video and a dashboard thumbnail.
No direct runtime interaction is visible because the media is paused.
impact_rationale: Second-hand buyers and sellers have a recognizable time and negotiation burden, and agent bargaining could provide useful convenience while preserving consent.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies online haggling and deal discovery as the target problem.
Human final approval is explicit.
creativity_rationale: Two-sided agent negotiation with human deal approval is a fresh extension of commerce automation, though the underlying marketplace concept is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Both buyer and seller agents participate in negotiation.
Approval/auto-approval policy is part of the workflow.
usability_note: Approval-oriented dashboard appears understandable, but the negotiation flow is not demonstrated.
red_flags: No submitted video frame sheets or transcript.
Only a paused Devpost preview supports the claimed workflow.
standouts: Two-sided negotiation and human deal gate are clear product hooks.
advance_reason: Interesting commerce use case, but evidence and WebMCP delta are not strong enough.
